pairs.reason: Claim 1 revokes general exclusions effective March 12, 2025. Claim 2 provides a specific exception for US-sourced derivatives subject to duties on or after that same date. The exception does not contradict the revocation of general exemptions; it defines a new scope of eligibility.

Claim 1 states tariffs do not stack. Claim 2 states that Section 232 tariffs and other additional tariffs can apply to the same product based on content, implying stacking is possible under specific guidance from June and July.

Claim 1 states goods with multiple metals are subject to only one rate (no stacking). Claim 2 states that Section 232 tariffs and other additional tariffs can apply to the same product based on content, suggesting multiple rates may apply.

Claim 1 announces the initiation of investigations on February 16, 2026. Claim 2 explains the relevance of that specific investigation to US exporters. The claims describe the same event and its implications without contradiction.

Claim 1 lists the duty rate for India. Claim 2 lists the same rate for India while adding rates for Indonesia and Thailand. The claims are consistent, with the second providing a more comprehensive list.
Claim 1 lists rates for Indonesia, Thailand, Ukraine, and Taiwan. Claim 2 lists rates for Thailand, Ukraine, and Taiwan. The second claim is a subset of the first, showing no contradiction.

Claim 1 cites a preliminary determination rate of 7.42 percent for the group. Claim 2 provides specific margin ranges (3.97-7.33% to 49.05%) for individual countries within that group. The specific ranges are consistent with the general preliminary finding.

Claim 1 refers to a general 25% rate for primary steel with potential exemptions. Claim 2 refers to a specific 10% tariff on derivatives composed of at least 85% US-sourced materials. The claims address different product categories and rates.

Claim 1 states a 10% tariff applies to the full value of derivatives. Claim 2 states the tariff applies only to the steel content, not the entire value. These represent contradictory bases for calculating the duty.

Claim 1 concerns the rescission of an administrative review for a specific period (Dec 2024-Nov 2025). Claim 2 concerns the continuation of orders effective May 13, 2026. These address different procedural stages and effective dates.
